reproduce.title: Hotkeys stopped working (possibly due to conflicts? but not shown in PowerToys)
reproduce.version_requirement: Reported Windows 11 25H2/update configuration and current supported PowerToys
prerequisites: Use the reported low-level-hook setting and configured Win+Space/Win+V shortcuts.
Keep the utility configuration fixed between attempts.
reproduce.expected_result: The first intended CmdPal invocation is distinguished from the Windows handler; no retracted workaround is treated as a fix.
steps: After reboot, press Win+Space once and record which UI appears; repeat once.
Repeat with Win+V, recording Windows UI and CmdPal activation separately.
Capture maintainer-side shortcut dispatch/activation traces for first and second press; compare without changing several settings together.

known_information: Win+Space and Win+V require another press while the Windows action wins the first one.
The report already supplies Windows/update details and a diagnostic archive; hook and administrator settings were tried.
A later reboot disproved the claim that re-enabling other utilities fixed it.

inferences: Input-hook ordering or activation state may allow the first reserved shortcut through; an empty conflict list does not prove Windows has not reserved it.
issue_context.summary: Command Palette shortcuts conflict with Windows handling on the first press; an earlier workaround was explicitly retracted.
issue_context.analysis: The current reproduction is sufficient for maintainer investigation. Remove the retracted workaround as a fix and do not request the same OS/build/ZIP again.

title: Hotkeys stopped working (possibly due to conflicts? but not shown in PowerToys)

confidence.rationale: The retracted workaround rules out a claimed fix but does not isolate hook ordering versus Windows-reserved behavior.

plan: Reproduce both Win+Space and Win+V from a fresh PowerToys launch without changing the existing utility configuration.
Trace whether the registered hook receives/consumes each first and second keydown and whether CmdPal activation is requested.
Correct the confirmed activation/registration boundary without globally suppressing Windows shortcuts when CmdPal does not own them.
proposed_fixes.title: Isolate first-press shortcut activation
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The first key sequence may pass through before the active shortcut handler consumes it; Windows-reserved handling and hook ordering remain competing explanations.
verification: A first intended invocation consistently opens CmdPal, or an explicitly unsupported reserved shortcut is rejected with clear behavior.
Verify unrelated Windows shortcuts remain available and reboot does not regress the behavior.
